title: High CO2 while asleep, not waking, watch changed

story.en: A crewmate is asleep in her cabin. The cabin CO2 1-hour average rises above the NASA limit of 3 mmHg. The system alerts her and reads the watches of everyone in the room at the same time. She does not wake. Her watch shows breathing above her normal, heart rate more than 20% above her baseline, and blood oxygen below 95%.
story.pt: A tripulante está dormindo no quarto. A média de 1 hora de CO2 do quarto passa do limite da NASA, de 3 mmHg. O sistema avisa a tripulante e confere o relógio de todos no cômodo ao mesmo tempo. Ela não acorda. O relógio mostra respiração acima do normal dela, batimento mais de 20% acima do basal e oxigênio no sangue abaixo de 95%.

readings.compared: above this person's normal and above 20
more than 20% above this person's baseline (about 52 bpm asleep)

must_not: suggest a diagnosis (for example coma or acidosis)

why: She did not wake while the CO2 is over the limit and her watch shows changed breathing, heart rate and oxygen. This suggests loss of consciousness and a risk of cardiorespiratory arrest, so everyone aboard is alerted.
notes: Rules from the medical lead, 14 Nov. System alerts the person and checks the watch of everyone in the room at the same time (no waiting). Watch changed means: respiratory rate above personal normal OR above 20; heart rate more than 20% or 20 bpm above personal baseline; SpO2 below 95. Reference tables she pasted have no named source: unverified. Test values are invented for the case.

title: High CO2 while asleep, not waking, watch normal

story.en: A crewmate is asleep in her cabin. The cabin CO2 1-hour average rises above the NASA limit of 3 mmHg. The system alerts her and reads the watches of everyone in the room at the same time. She does not wake, but her watch shows no change: breathing, heart rate and blood oxygen are within her normal and the reference values.
story.pt: A tripulante está dormindo no quarto. A média de 1 hora de CO2 do quarto passa do limite da NASA, de 3 mmHg. O sistema avisa a tripulante e confere o relógio de todos no cômodo ao mesmo tempo. Ela não acorda, mas o relógio não mostra alteração: respiração, batimento e oxigênio estão dentro do normal dela e dos valores de referência.

readings.compared: within this person's normal and below 20
within this person's baseline (about 52 bpm asleep)

must_not: suggest a diagnosis (for example coma or acidosis)

why: She is not waking while the CO2 is over the limit. Her vital signs are normal, so it may be heavy sleep, but with the room air this bad it can get serious within minutes. Prevention: alert the nearest roommate to wake her, fix the room CO2 and start the card steps.
notes: Rule from the medical lead, 14 Nov: concerning, and also notify the nearest roommate to wake her; 'notify' has no roommate value, so it is self here and the roommate is in this note. Not yet decided: whether the medical officer is also notified at this level. The system keeps reading the watch; if it changes, it becomes case-001 (dangerous, everyone). Test values are invented. Approved by the medical lead without a medical officer alert at this level (she did not ask for it).

title: Headache with CO2 below the NASA limit

story.en: A crewmate in her cabin reports a headache. The cabin CO2 1-hour average is 2.6 mmHg: above 2.3 (where NASA reports first symptoms) but still under the NASA limit of 3 mmHg. The system points to the room as something to check.
story.pt: A tripulante está no quarto e relata dor de cabeça. A média de 1 hora de CO2 do quarto é 2,6 mmHg: acima de 2,3 (onde a NASA relata os primeiros sintomas), mas ainda abaixo do limite da NASA, de 3 mmHg. O sistema aponta o quarto como algo a verificar.

readings.compared: above 2.3, below the NASA limit of 3

why: NASA reports first symptoms from 2.3 mmHg, so a headache here can be the room. The crewmate is told to move to another room and follow the CO2 card steps.
notes: Medical lead, 14 Nov: 2.3 mmHg is the number, but even a little lower, if there are symptoms, the card steps should already be followed. How much lower is not decided yet. Shown as exposure to check, never as the cause. Test values are invented. She added: this applies to mild symptoms (the mild list in the CO2 card: headache, sleepiness, hand tremor, flushing, sweating). Final: the number is 2.3 mmHg, no lower cutoff.

title: Headache with normal CO2: no warning, only questions

story.en: A crewmate in her cabin reports a headache. The cabin CO2 is normal (0.5 mmHg, below 2.3). Her watch is within her normal. The system gives no warning and asks light questions about sleep, water and food.
story.pt: A tripulante está no quarto e relata dor de cabeça. O CO2 do quarto está normal (0,5 mmHg, abaixo de 2,3). O relógio está dentro do normal dela. O sistema não dá aviso e faz perguntas leves sobre sono, água e comida.

expected.next_question: Did you sleep well last night? Did you drink water today? Did you eat today?

why: Nothing points to the room or the body: CO2 is normal and the watch is normal. A headache alone is common, so the system only asks about sleep, water and food.
notes: Medical lead, 14 Nov: all three questions. What the system does with the answers is not decided. Test values are invented.
